body: Can you come up with a use case in which you would want to look up this nonexistent associated object?

This stems from the change where an error is now raised, but `#valid?` happens to one method that does **not** handle that error when there are some custom validations on its assocations, but a lot of find methods rescue this error.
https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/e62fff40edde10bd04bbb91ce242f4a7f7ea64a8

This is actually a bigger problem in general with any integer backed column and validation.  
Any value larger than the db column can handle that is assigned to an attribute will raise an `RangeError` if `#valid?` is called from the model.  The whole point of `valid?` is to return true/false so this breaks the intended behavior of the method.

Unfortunately, we have had to write custom validations that `rescue` those errors, which should have not been unnecessary.  I hope this gets fixed.

The specifics of our uses cases have been around custom validations of the existence of such values in another model and also have a validation using `less_than_or_equal_to`.  But the custom validation results with a DB query which then gets a `RangeError` because of the invalid cast value for the DB.

It would seem that validations in general might need to rescue that error or at least maybe only from `#valid?` ?.

issue.title: Prevent raising RangeError in AR presence validation [4-2-stable]

After updating ActiveRecord version to 4.2 in my application I noticed a strange behavior. If I call `#valid?` method for an ActiveRecord model, it may raise an unexpected `RangeError` exception. For example:

After updating ActiveRecord version from 4.1 in my application I noticed a strange behavior. If I call `#valid?` method for an ActiveRecord model, it may raise an unexpected `RangeError` exception. For example:

issue.title: Prevent `RangeError` for `belongs_to` associations
issue.body:
Currently to access `belongs_to` associations raises a `RangeError` if
foreign key attribute has out of range value.
It should return a nil value rather than raising a `RangeError`.

Fixes #20140.
